title: Technology Sector Update for 05/03/2018: LOGI,NSIT,CRUS
text:

GOOG -0.29%
Technology stocks were retreating Thursday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing almost 0.8% in value while the Philadelphia semiconductor index also was posting a nearly 0.8% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Logitech International ( LOGI ) climbed almost 10% on Thursday after the computer peripherals company exceeded analyst estimates with its Q1 financial results. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.32 per share during the three months ended March 31, up from $0.30 per share during the same quarter last year and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.08 per share. Revenue rose to $592.4 million from $510.6 million last year, also beating the $560.4 million analyst mean. Logitech Thursday also confirmed its FY19 outlook expecting sales growth in the high single percentage digits and non-GAAP operating income in a range of $310 million to $320 million. in non-GAAP operating income. Analysts, on average, are expecting FY18 sales at the company to rise 14.1% over the prior 12-month period to around $2.53 billion.
In other sector news:
+ Insight Enterprises ( NSIT ) soared nearly 23% at one point during Thursday trading after reporting Q1 net income and revenue exceeding Wall Street estimates and raising its FY18 earnings forecast above Street views. Excluding one-time items, the enterprise software firm earned $0.94 per share, up 68% over year-ago levels and topping the Capital IQ consensus for normalized earnings by $0.60 per share. GAAP net income for the January-to-March fiscal period more than doubled compared with the same quarter last year, rising 137% to $0.90 per share and breezing past the $0.58 per share analyst mean. Net sales rose 19% year over year to $1.76 billion, also topping the $1.53 billion consensus call. Looking forward, Insight increased its projected FY18 EPS outlook by $0.45 compared with its prior forecast to a new range of $4.35 to $4.45 per share, surpassing the consensus estimate by at least $0.39 per share.
+ Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) has turned slightly higher Thursday afternoon, erasing a nearly 9% decline earlier that followed the fabless chipmaker reporting below-consensus fiscal Q4 financial results and forecasting revenue for the current quarter also trailing Wall Street expectations. Excluding one-time items, it earned $0.51 per share, down from $0.85 per share last year and missing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.07 per share. Revenue fell to $303.2 million from $327.9 million last year and also lagging the $316.6 million Street view. For the current quarter, the company is modelling Q1 revenue between $210 million to $250 million. Analysts, on average, are looking for $294.7 million in revenue in the April-to-June reporting period.
